description: KERNEL GROWTH (Stage 2, L0) — the agent GROWS its own visual receptive fields from image statistics, instead of selecting from a hand-designed pool. This seed exists because the Stage-1 floor did NOT do this: sensory_convolution ships six designed:1.0 kernels (onset/offset/edge_axis1/centre_surround/diagonal/smoother), NO rule anywhere mints a Kernel, and keep_discriminative_kernel only SELECTS (it keeps whatever responds variably across fields — an injected garbage kernel is kept just as readily). So 'center-surround and oriented kernels emerged from image statistics' was, in the floor, finding what the seed had planted. These two rules close that gap: a kernel is MINTED from a real unexplained image patch (its initial weights ARE image structure, never a designed template) and then LEARNS by Oja's rule against the image stream. Whether biological structure (center-surround / oriented) actually emerges is then an OPEN, FALSIFIABLE measurement over real data — not an assumption baked into the pool.

microtheory.name: vision_growth
microtheory.description: receptive fields are grown, not designed: mint-on-residual (an unexplained patch becomes a new kernel) + Oja's rule (local Hebbian learning with self-normalisation) driven by the image stream, all inside the run_rules fixpoint

attrs.name: default
attrs.comment: Growth knobs as GRAPH DATA (tunable, no Python literal). eta: Oja learning rate. novelty_threshold: a patch is UNEXPLAINED (mint a kernel for it) when the best held kernel's |response| is below novelty_threshold x the patch's own magnitude — a scale-aware residual test, so it does not fire merely because a patch is bright. min_contrast: a patch must carry real structure (Magnitude > this) before it can mint or teach — blank sky must not become a receptive field. max_kernels: the pool cap (growth is bounded, and the cap being REACHED is itself a reportable fact). kh/kw: the receptive-field size the world adapter slices patches at; a grown kernel's weights ARE a patch, so these must agree.

rules.name: vg_mint_kernel_from_patch
rules.comment: MINT-ON-RESIDUAL (the vf_contradiction_split / sd_mint_quantum shape, pointed at Kernel). A patch that (a) carries real structure and (b) is NOT explained by any held kernel (best |Dot(w,x)| < novelty_threshold x |x| — scale-aware, so the test is about SHAPE agreement, not brightness) becomes a new Kernel whose weights ARE that patch. This is the honest sense of 'grown from image statistics': the receptive field is initialised out of real image structure the agent could not already account for, never from a designed template. ConvFaculty -has_kernel-> Kernel is already a declared sensory_convolution production, so the minted kernel joins the candidate pool with no schema change and keep_discriminative_kernel picks it up unmodified. Terminates: mint_checked is set only on the patch that actually minted (once per patch), the pool is capped by max_kernels, and a patch already explained by the pool never fires at all.

rules.name: vg_learn_kernel_oja
rules.comment: OJA'S RULE, GRAPH-NATIVE — the learning step, inside the run_rules fixpoint (the same 'the net trains itself as the graph collapses' posture as net_collapse, but at the right shape for a receptive field). w <- w(1 - eta*y^2) + eta*y*x, with y = Dot(w, x). Plain Hebbian (w += eta*y*x) diverges; Oja's decay term is what self-normalises it, and it is the textbook local rule whose fixed point is the leading principal component of the input a unit wins — the biologically-plausible route to a receptive field. Expressible with NO new Rust because the update factors into two scalar-x-vector maps plus a VecAdd: MapList binds its var ON TOP of the existing env, so the outer match vars (k, p) and the scalar y stay in scope inside the map. WINNER-TAKE-ALL (Eq(k, Argmax over the pool of |response|)) is what makes the pool DIVERSIFY rather than every unit collapsing onto the same first component: each patch teaches only the kernel that already best explains it, so units specialise (competitive learning). Only grown:1.0 kernels learn — a designed kernel, if any is present, is left exactly as seeded, so the two populations never mix in a measurement. Terminates: the `learned` marker makes it exactly ONE Oja step per patch per ingest; the stream (more frames -> more patches) is what supplies more steps.
